title: A Mini Structured Safety Case Template Stress-Tested With Real Eval Data

original_idea.body:
# A Mini Structured Safety Case Template Stress-Tested With Real Eval Data

**Problem:** Apollo argues for structured safety cases that AI is unlikely to scheme, but these are mostly conceptual. There is no lightweight, reproducible worked example that plugs concrete open-model eval numbers into a safety-case argument and exposes where the argument breaks.

**Direction:** Pick one narrow scheming claim (e.g., 'this model will not sandbag on capability X'). Build a small structured argument (claims -> evidence -> assumptions) and instantiate it with real measurements from a small open model (sandbagging tests, eval-awareness probe results). Then adversarially attack each assumption with a cheap experiment and document which links fail.

**Why it matters:** Turns abstract safety-case methodology into a concrete, criticizable artifact that others can reuse — strategically valuable safety infrastructure. Building safety cases against scheming is an explicit Apollo open problem.

**Relevant context:** apolloresearch.ai 'Towards Safety Cases for AI Scheming' (research agenda in context file). Uses open-model eval outputs and the eval-awareness/sandbagging methods above; no training, no lab infra.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: concrete criticizable safety-case artifact against scheming (explicit Apollo problem).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building a structured argument + instantiating with evals + adversarial attacks needs research maturity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Deliverable requires sustained multi-workstream effort (argument + several eval experiments).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly safety infra; labs underinvest in worked safety cases.

novelty.reasoning: Safety cases for scheming are conceptual; a worked instantiated mini-case appears novel.
